newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Foreigners can put $78.7 bln more in Taiwan stocks.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners can put $78.7 bln more in Taiwan stocks.

text.p: Foreign investors can put US$78.731 billion more into Taiwan's stock market before hitting an official ceiling, the central bank said on Saturday.
As of May 7, foreign investors are allowed to invest a total of $90.381 billion in Taiwan's stock market, or 25 percent of the market's total market value, the bank said in a statement.
Foreign funds had a net outflow of $102.496 million between May 1 and 7, with some $128.121 million flowing into Taiwan and $230.617 million flowing out of the island, the statement said.
In April, foreign funds registered a net inflow of $164.813 million.
Taiwan also set a ceiling of $3 billion for funds raised overseas by local firms through convertible bonds and global depositary receipts.
Of the category, foreigners as of May 7 can still put $1.162 billion more into the island, the bank said.
